tagline: Fix broken, malformed or LLM-mangled JSON into valid JSON instantly
pageDescription: Repair broken and malformed JSON with this free online JSON Repair tool. It fixes the most common problems automatically — trailing commas, single quotes, unquoted keys, missing brackets, comments, Python-style None/True/False and truncated or markdown-wrapped output from ChatGPT and other LLMs — then returns clean, valid, pretty-printed JSON. Everything runs in your browser with no signup and no upload, so even sensitive payloads stay private. Perfect for developers debugging API responses, cleaning AI output and rescuing config files.

instructions.title: How to repair broken JSON

steps.title: Paste your broken JSON
steps.description: Drop in the malformed JSON — it can include single quotes, trailing commas, comments or even a ```json code fence.

steps.title: Choose the indentation
steps.description: Pick 2 or 4 spaces, tabs, or minified output depending on how you want the repaired JSON formatted.

steps.title: Click Repair JSON
steps.description: The tool fixes the syntax, re-parses the result and pretty-prints guaranteed-valid JSON.

steps.title: Review the result
steps.description: Check the repaired JSON. If it was already valid you'll see a note that it was only reformatted.

steps.title: Copy the clean JSON
steps.description: Click Copy to grab the valid JSON and paste it straight into your code, config or API client.

proTips: Paste the whole ```json block — the fence is stripped automatically
Truncated LLM output is closed with matching brackets, but verify the data
Use minified output to shrink JSON for storage or transport
If the repair looks wrong, the source was ambiguous — fix it slightly and retry
Need to compare versions? Pair with a JSON diff tool
Everything is local, so you can repair private payloads safely
troubleshooting: Could not repair: the input is too far from JSON — fix obvious typos and retry
Numbers turned into strings: they were quoted in the source; remove the quotes
Output is just a string: bare text becomes a JSON string — wrap it in {} if you meant an object
Lost a comment: JSON has no comments, so they're removed by design
Keys reordered: object key order is preserved; only formatting changes
